about.title: Escalon Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Escalon is a small, close-knit agricultural community, but defective products cause the same kinds of harm here as anywhere else — whether it's a piece of farm equipment that fails, a faulty vehicle part on Rt 120 or McHenry Avenue, a malfunctioning power tool, or a household item that catches fire. California's product liability law generally applies strict liability, meaning an injured person usually doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product had a defect in its design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that the defect caused the injury. Liability can extend to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. Because these cases often hinge on physical evidence, preserving the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident matters. If you or someone you love was hurt by a product in Escalon, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who reviews defective product claims and works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law frequently allows claims under strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product was defective and whether that defect caused your injury, rather than on the manufacturer's conduct.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it may be key evidence in your claim.
